prompt.context: Your client is a large, global diversified company. Some of their businesses include consumer products, steel refining, and financial services. Currently they are organized in a matrix fashion, with operating units reporting to both business line heads and country managers. However, the operating units have developed considerable autonomy and often play the country managers off the business line heads. As a result, the company is operating as 200 independent companies.
prompt.question: The CEO wants to reorganize the company into 'Natural Business Units' or functional silos. He wants to know: (1) How he can ensure that synergies across business units are still leveraged, and (2) How he can convince his managers to work together to extract synergies.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any additional information available about the specific synergies that exist across business units?

exhibits.title: Current Organizational Structure
exhibits.shows: A matrix diagram showing the current organizational structure with Business Lines (A, B, C, D, E) on one axis and Country Managers (W, X, Y, Z) on the other axis, with Operating Units at each intersection
exhibits.data: Business Lines: A, B, C, D, E; Country Managers: W, X, Y, Z; each cell represents an Operating Unit

exhibits.title: Proposed Organizational Structure and Spectrum of Work
exhibits.shows: A diagram showing the proposed organizational structure with Business Lines reorganized into Groups A, B, C under a CEO, alongside a 'Spectrum of Work' bar illustrating three categories of work across business units
exhibits.data: Proposed structure: CEO at top, Group A, Group B, Group C below; Spectrum of Work categories: Common Functions (e.g. purchasing, technology), Potential Synergies (e.g. Marketing), Unique Work (e.g. manufacturing)

framework: Step 1: Identify what synergies exist across the business units
Step 2: Define metrics to evaluate how business heads work to extract synergies with other business units
Step 3: Put incentives in place to reward synergy-seeking behavior

questions.prompt: How would you identify synergies across business units in the new structure?
questions.guidance: Use the Spectrum of Work framework. Work can be classified into three categories: (1) Common Functions — easiest to group together for economies of scale/scope (e.g., purchasing, technology); (2) Potential Synergies — require analysis to identify (e.g., marketing); (3) Unique Work — no synergy possible (e.g., manufacturing). For Potential Synergies, evaluate customer overlap across business units. For example, if the Steel Unit and Financial Services both make loans to medium-sized businesses, there are likely synergies to exploit.

questions.prompt: How would you create buy-in among executives for the new structure and for cooperating to extract synergies?
questions.guidance: The CEO must demonstrate concrete benefits of cooperation to his executives: (1) Potential cost savings from common functions (economies of scale); (2) Potential increased revenue or profits from bundling products across business units. These tangible benefits make the case for why executives should collaborate rather than operate independently.

questions.prompt: How would you define metrics to measure synergy extraction?
questions.guidance: Metrics may need to be subjective or use 360-degree reviews from other business units to assess the degree of cooperation and synergy extraction. Standard financial KPIs alone are insufficient because synergies are cross-unit; peer feedback from other business unit heads provides a more complete picture.

questions.prompt: How would you structure the incentive system to drive synergy-seeking behavior?
questions.guidance: Performance against 'synergy metrics' must be explicitly included in executives' compensation packages. Without financial incentives tied to synergy metrics, executives in the new functional silo structure have no personal motivation to cooperate across units. The incentive structure gives the new organizational design real teeth.

brainstorming.prompt: What types of synergies might exist across the business units (consumer products, steel refining, financial services) of this diversified company?

categories.name: Common Functions (Cost Synergies)
ideas: Centralized purchasing / procurement across all units
Shared IT infrastructure and technology platforms
Common HR and talent acquisition functions
Consolidated real estate and facilities management

categories.name: Potential Revenue Synergies
ideas: Cross-selling financial services products to steel and consumer product customers
Bundling consumer products with financing offers from financial services unit
Shared marketing and brand-building for overlapping customer segments
Joint go-to-market for medium-sized business customers (e.g., steel loans + financial services loans)

categories.name: Knowledge and Capability Synergies
ideas: Shared analytics and data capabilities across customer-facing units
Best practice sharing in supply chain management
Common leadership development programs leveraging scale

categories.name: Capital Allocation Synergies
ideas: Internal capital markets — profitable units fund growth of others
Diversified cash flow reduces external borrowing costs

recommendation: Proceed with the reorganization into Natural Business Units (functional silos) while building an explicit synergy management layer
Immediately map the Spectrum of Work across all units to identify Common Functions (consolidate for cost savings) and Potential Synergies (evaluate via customer overlap analysis)
Establish cross-unit synergy metrics — including 360-degree peer reviews — and tie a meaningful portion of executive compensation to performance against these metrics
risks: Executives in functional silos may still resist cooperation if incentives are insufficient or poorly designed
Subjective metrics for synergy performance may create disputes or be gamed
Identifying true synergies in a highly diversified portfolio (consumer products, steel, financial services) may be limited — not all units have natural overlap
Transition period may be disruptive as 200 autonomous operating units are consolidated
next_steps: Conduct a detailed Spectrum of Work mapping across all 200 operating units
Analyze customer bases of each unit to identify Potential Synergy areas
Design the synergy metrics framework and compensation structure with HR and executive input
Pilot the new structure in one region before global rollout
